Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-11-25

Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Raj Patel (Cobalt PM), Zoe Kim (Cobalt Data Eng), Marcus Lee (Cobalt CTO)

Summary (auto): Customer exploring Redwood for embeddings + reranking. Key constraints: throughput, latency, data residency (PII), and rerank accuracy. Next: share benchmarks + security docs, start POC with 10k sample docs.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya, AE on the account, and with me is Liam our solutions engineer. we wanted to run through your current search stack and the rerank flow you mentioned.
[00:48] Raj Patel: thanks. quick context — we are Cobalt Systems, we run a knowledge search over about 1M docs, mix of product docs and support tickets, some PII in notes. current infra is elasticsearch + a FAISS offline index, but it's messy. goal is better recall and a reranker for precision.
[02:05] Liam O'Connor: got it. a typical pattern we see is embed at write time, store vectors in a vector DB like pinecone or redis vector; do ANN search for topK, then run a cross-encoder reranker for final ordering. for throughput on 1M docs we usually tune shard counts and embedding dims. what's your current QPS and latency target?
[04:10] Zoe Kim: peak query rates around 300 QPS on search endpoints, but not all requests need rerank. our tight path is a support rep workflow where we need top-3 within 150-200ms end-to-end. that's the tricky bit.
[06:15] Marcus Lee: and we have regula — regulatory needs around PII, so hosted is okay for dev, but for prod we might need dedicated or private (VPC/on-prem). also SOC2 and audit logs are mandatory.
[08:20] Maya Chen: totally makes sense. hosted is the fastest to get started, but Dedicated gives predictable throughput and Private gives you the VPC + on-prem options and KMS/HSM integrations. we do have SOC2 + ISO docs — i'll make sure liam shares them.
[10:30] Raj Patel: can you speak to dimensionality? our ML team is split — some prefer 1536-length embeddings (open models) for accuracy, others push 768 for storage/cost. tradeoffs?
[12:40] Liam O'Connor: yes — higher dim often helps recall/semantic nuance, but doubles storage and increases vector DB I/O and compute for similarity. at 1M docs 1536 vectors are fine on dedicated infra, but if cost is a big driver 768 or quantized 1536 can be good. also consider hybrid search: keep BM25 filters for exact matches and run lower-dim vectors for speed, then rerank with a cross-encoder to recover precision.
[14:50] Zoe Kim: hybrid sounds appealing, we already have Elasticsearch so adding BM25 + vector overlay should be straightforward. any gotchas integrating pinecone vs redis vs milvus?
[17:00] Liam O'Connor: pinecone is managed — easy to start, but cost at scale can be higher. redis vector is fast and can sit in your VPC, but you need ops ownership. milvus / faiss are good for self-hosted clusters. important levers: index type (IVF vs HNSW), quantization (PQ), and number of probes. also sharding strategy for throughput. we occasionally see mis-transcripts where people say "k V cache" but mean KV cache — caching prefix results can cut repeated token cost.
[19:10] Raj Patel: for reranker we want GPU cross-encoder to stay under 200ms for topK=10. what does Redwood recommend for model selection and serving?
[21:20] Liam O'Connor: typical pattern: CPU for embeddings unless using a big transformer, and GPU for cross-encoder rerank. with Redwood Dedicated you can reserve GPU pools and configure autoscaling so your reranker stays in that 150-250ms tail. we can run microbenchmarks — e.g., cross-encoder 3B model on A10-like instance gives X ms per query for batch size N — we'll share numbers.
[23:30] Marcus Lee: curious about batching and latency tradeoffs — we need predictable p95. can Redwood do per-route SLOs and fallback strategies?
[25:40] Maya Chen: yes, per-route model pinning, canary rollouts, and policy-based routing. for p95 latency we can set autoscale and fallback to a smaller reranker or degrade gracefully by skipping rerank for non-critical calls. Redwood Optimize can recommend batching configs to meet cost vs latency goals.
[27:50] Zoe Kim: storage/throughput question: we expect 1M vectors ~1536 dim — ballpark storage? and does Redwood count storage or is that on customer vector DB?
[30:00] Liam O'Connor: storage is typically in your vector DB; Redwood Hosted can include managed vector store options depending on plan. rough estimate: float32 1536 x 1M ~ 6GB*? wait, no — math: 1536*4 bytes=6,144 bytes per vector -> ~6.1MB per 1K -> ~6.1GB per 1M (actually ~6.1GB). with metadata overhead and index structures you're closer to 10-12GB. quantized 8-bit / PQ will reduce ~4x.
[32:10] Raj Patel: thanks, that clarifies. on data residency — if we go hosted, can we restrict region and get audit logs + retention controls?
[34:20] Liam O'Connor: hosted supports region restrictions and we emit audit logs, retention controls, and can integrate with your KMS for key management on Dedicated/Private. for strict PII controls Private or on-prem is recommended.
[36:30] Zoe Kim: about integration — do you have SDK examples for node/python, and sample code for the embed -> topK -> rerank pipeline?
[38:40] Maya Chen: yes, we have SDKs and a reference repo. i'll drop links after the call. we've got a sample rerank notebook that uses pinecone + cross-encoder, and one for redis.
[40:50] Marcus Lee: what about cost modeling? curious how Redwood prices embedding ops vs rerank GPU time and vector storage.
[43:00] Liam O'Connor: hosted is usage-based: per-embedding/token and per-rerank call depending on model size. Dedicated is capacity reservations which smooths unit cost and gives SLA. for POC we'll do an estimate based on your 300 QPS peak and expected ratio of rerank calls. we'll include a cost spreadsheet.
[45:10] Raj Patel: any customer refs doing similar scale? we'd like to talk to someone in fintech with PII constraints if possible.
[47:20] Maya Chen: yes, we can connect you with two customers; i'll include that in the follow-up along with the benchmark sheet and SOC2 + SSO docs. thanks everyone, we'll follow up on next steps in the notes.
